title: Rays Walk Off in 12th Inning to Keep World Series Alive
dek: Ben Williamson's single in the bottom of the 12th gave Tampa Bay a 4-3 win over the Brewers in Game 4, forcing a Game 5 with Milwaukee still holding a 3-1 series lead.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Interior view of Tropicana Field, the Tampa Bay Rays' home ballpark, from the upper deck

keyPoints: The Rays beat the Brewers 4-3 in 12 innings at Tropicana Field on Tuesday night, avoiding a World Series sweep.
Cooper Pratt's solo home run in the 12th put Milwaukee ahead, but Tampa Bay tied it on a throwing error and a DeLuca single, then won it on Ben Williamson's walk-off single.
Milwaukee still leads the series 3-1, and Game 5 is set for Wednesday.
body:
The Tampa Bay Rays kept their World Series hopes alive on Tuesday night, beating the Milwaukee Brewers 4-3 in 12 innings at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida. The win forces a Game 5 and leaves the Brewers one win from the title.

## A tie game into extra innings

The game was tightly contested, closer to Games 1 and 2 than the high-scoring Game 3, according to CBS Sports. David Hamilton's home run in the fifth inning tied the score at 2-2, and it stayed level until the 12th. CBS Sports described it as Hamilton's second home run of the postseason. ESPN's box score shows Milwaukee with eight hits and Tampa Bay with nine.

In the top of the 12th, Cooper Pratt hit a go-ahead solo home run to left-center, and the Brewers were three outs from the title. The Rays answered in the bottom half. A leadoff throwing error by third baseman Joey Ortiz put Tampa Bay's first runner on, Jonny DeLuca singled in the tying run, and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson then singled over first baseman Jake Bauers to end the game.

## Series context

CBS Sports reported that the Rays are the first team to avoid elimination in a World Series with a walk-off win since David Freese's heroics for the St. Louis Cardinals in Game 6 in 2011. Tampa Bay used starter Nick Martinez and closer Bryan Baker for two innings each in relief, the first two-inning appearance for Baker since July 9, 2024, CBS Sports noted. That workload leaves questions for Game 5.

Milwaukee's Jacob Misiorowski is the pitcher the Rays will face next, and Rays manager Kevin Cash said after the game that the team wanted to enjoy the win but refocus quickly against a strong starter, according to CBS Sports.

## The box score and the crowd

ESPN listed the game at Tropicana Field with an attendance of 40,514 and a game time of 4 hours, 20 minutes. Coverage was on Fox. ESPN's box score lists I. Seymour as the winning pitcher and S. Drohan as the losing pitcher.

## What comes next

The Brewers lead the best-of-seven series 3-1. Game 5 is scheduled for Wednesday, Oct. 28. A Tampa Bay win would cut the Brewers' series lead to 3-2 and force a Game 6. A Milwaukee win would end the series.
